identity.title: Diffusion Language Model Knows the Answer Before It Decodes

problem.claim: DLM inference is slowed by bidirectional-attention costs and many refinement steps needed for high-quality outputs.

gap.claim: The authors identify early answer convergence as an overlooked property that existing DLM decoding does not exploit.

contributions.claim: Prophet is a training-free early-commit decoding paradigm that dynamically stops refinement or decodes all remaining tokens in one step using the top-2 confidence gap.
Prophet integrates with existing DLM implementations with negligible overhead and no additional training.
The work reframes DLM decoding as deciding when to stop sampling, based on early answer convergence.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present exploiting early answer convergence through Prophet's early-commit decoding as their new contribution.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that up to 97% of GSM8K instances and 99% of MMLU instances can be decoded correctly using half the refinement steps.
Across tasks on LLaDA-8B and Dream-7B, the authors report up to 3.4× fewer decoding steps while preserving high generation quality.
The authors report additional speedups when Prophet is combined with existing acceleration methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: DLMs offer parallel generation and flexible token orders, but inference remains slower because of attention costs and many refinement steps.
The authors report that correct answers often converge internally by halfway through refinement under semi-autoregressive and random-remasking schedules.
Prophet uses a top-2 confidence gap to decide between continued refinement and committing all remaining tokens at once.
On LLaDA-8B and Dream-7B, the authors report substantial step reductions while maintaining high generation quality and gaining further speedups with other accelerators.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects a measurable intermediate-state behavior—early answer convergence—to a stopping rule based on the top-2 confidence gap.

lessons.interpretation: A useful acceleration idea can emerge by measuring when the target-relevant state stabilizes, rather than optimizing every generation step uniformly.
lessons.application: For an iterative generator, track answer stability and define an explicit confidence-based early-exit criterion.
lessons.exception: This may be unsuitable when answers lack identifiable regions or when confidence gaps are poorly calibrated during refinement.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify how the confidence-gap threshold is selected or calibrated.
The reported speedup conditions, quality metrics, task counts, and comparison baselines are not given.
The abstract does not quantify the additional speedups from combining Prophet with other acceleration methods.
